title: Pharmacist-led follow-up for patients starting oral anticancer agents: a rapid review for a funding decision
subtitle: Adherence, harms and dose intensity, and staff time and money, reported as separate strands
statement: About 480 patients a year start oral anticancer agents at the centre; 17 percent have an unplanned admission within 90 days, half for toxicity, and about one in five collect repeat supplies late. The drug and therapeutics committee must decide by February 2027 whether to fund a pharmacist-led follow-up service. A rapid review will summarise evidence on adherence (by measurement method), unplanned admissions and severe toxicity, dose intensity, pharmacist time, costs and patients' views, reported as separate strands.
whoAffected: Adults starting oral anticancer agents at home, especially older patients living alone, patients who need interpreters and patients far from the centre; oncology pharmacists and oncologists; the committee.
whatHurts: Toxicity recognised late leads to admissions and interrupted treatment; poor adherence can reduce benefit; a service funded on a misleading single figure could divert pharmacist time from other patients.
currentPractice: Oncology review every four to twelve weeks with no structured pharmacist follow-up between visits.
whyNow: The committee's funding round closes on 15 February 2027 and it asked for a report by 20 January.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients taking cancer treatment at home have toxicity recognised early and keep receiving the treatment they need, wherever they live and whatever language they speak.
summary: Problem framed as a rapid review for a funding decision, with separate strands for adherence, harms, and time and costs.
